"Come see about me" is a wellknown musical refrain, most famously recorded by The Supremes in 1964 and written by the Motown songwriting trio Holland–Dozier–Holland. It also appears as a prominent track by Nicki Minaj on her 2018 album Queen.[1][2][3]

 The Motown Classic

Recorded by The Supremes and led by Diana Ross, the 1964 single became the group's third consecutive numberone hit on the Billboard Hot 100.[4][5]

 The song features an upbeat, driving Motown tempo arranged by the Funk Brothers.[2]
 The narrative centers on romantic longing and vulnerability, as the narrator pleads for an estranged partner to return and reconcile.[6][2]
 The contrast between melancholy lyrics and energetic rhythm is a hallmark of Holland–Dozier–Holland's signature production style.[7][2]

 Modern Interpretations

Nicki Minaj released an emotional R&B ballad under the same title in 2018.[3]

 The track explores themes of regret, personal growth, and asking an expartner for another chance after drifting apart.[8][3]
 Rather than a rapid soul beat, it relies on a slower tempo focusing on the difficulty of maintaining relationships amidst highprofile careers.[3]
